glyph_origin: Originally an ideogram (指事) of a tiger with a line representing exhaled air while roaring, thus meaning "to roar; to shout". Later forms added 口 (“mouth”) or 言 (“speech”) to emphasize the act of crying or calling. 号 derives from 口 and the line 丂. In the current form, an ideogrammic compound (會意) and phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 号 (“to wail”) + semantic 虎 (“tiger”).
s_page_origin: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 口 (“mouth”) + 丂 (“exhaled air; a tiger's cry”). See 號 for more details.
senses: [háo] to shout; to bawl; to cry loudly
note: glyph_origin is from the traditional page 號; s_page_origin explains the simplified 号.
